newsitem.title: CHINA: China sets rules on stock-related asset appraisal.
newsitem.headline: China sets rules on stock-related asset appraisal.

text.p: China has issued new rules to boost control over asset appraisals involving listed firms and state companies preparing to list shares, the China Securities newspaper said on Tuesday.
The rules, issued by the National Administration of State Property, were aimed at strengthening management and preventing appraisal errors, the newspaper said without elaborating.
Asset appraisals must be carried out when state firms are turned into shareholding companies for future listings.
Asset appraisals are needed for any non-cash rights offers, mergers or ownership transfers, it said.

Appraisal agents should carry out assessments of listed firms' overall assets, including long-term investment, land-use rights, patent-use rights and intangible assets, it said without giving further details.
